soilBenefit.mustard: Deep taproot breaks the hard plough pan and enhances soil aeration; glucosinolate residues help suppress soil-borne pathogens. Does NOT fix atmospheric nitrogen.
soilBenefit.wheat: Produces substantial organic biomass and stubble; heavy feeder that requires nitrogen fertilizer, does NOT fix nitrogen.
soilBenefit.lentil: Legume nodules with Rhizobium bacteria fix 30–40 kg atmospheric nitrogen/ha, enriching topsoil for succeeding crops.
soilBenefit.boro_rice: Continuous flooded cultivation depletes topsoil aeration and depletes aquifer; minimal nitrogen fixation; requires heavy chemical fertilization.
soilBenefit.mungbean: Short-duration legume fixing 35–50 kg atmospheric nitrogen/ha. Deep roots and leafy biomass make it an excellent green manure.
soilBenefit.aus_rice: Early kharif semi-flooded cereal; utilizes pre-monsoon rains; does NOT fix nitrogen.
soilBenefit.aman_rice: Monsoon rainfed staple cereal; recycles straw organic matter into paddy soil; does NOT fix nitrogen.
soilBenefit.fallow: Natural resting interval; preserves residual soil moisture and allows beneficial microbial recovery.

waterNeed.mustard: Low irrigation (1–2 light waterings). Highly water efficient winter oilseed.
waterNeed.wheat: Moderate irrigation (2–3 scheduled waterings at crown root initiation and flowering).
waterNeed.lentil: Very low irrigation (1 light watering or residual soil moisture from monsoon).
waterNeed.boro_rice: Extremely high irrigation (20–25 heavy pumpings). Strains deep tube wells.
waterNeed.mungbean: Low irrigation (1 light watering or pre-monsoon showers).
waterNeed.aus_rice: Moderate irrigation (supplementary during early dry spells).
waterNeed.aman_rice: Rainfed (monsoon rains; requires 0–1 supplementary watering during drought).
